newsitem.title: CUBA: Cuba, Ecuador sign acord to fight drug trafficking.
newsitem.headline: Cuba, Ecuador sign acord to fight drug trafficking.

text.p: Cuba and Ecuador have signed an accord to cooperate on combatting drug trafficking in the region in Cuba's latest effort to stop the island from becoming a transit point for smuggling from Latin America.
Official media said on Thursday the accord was signed late on Wednesday by visiting Ecuadorean chief prosecutor Leonidas Plaza and Cuba's new Justice Minister Roberto Diaz.

The agreement, including provisions for exchange of information and training, added to bilateral accords on drug smuggling that Cuba has with some 15 other countries. Most recently, the Caribbean island has signed agreements with France and Britain.

Cuban authorities say they have seen a big rise this year in hauls of drugs such as cocaine from Cuban airports and also territorial waters. This is partly because the island is increasingly being used as a transit point for drugs smuggled from Latin American to Europe or North America, and partly because of more effective police and customs work, they say.
